./PHASE_4_DEMO_REALISM_REPORT.md-20-- **Large values:** High totals such as the 4.2k AI automation deployment, 3.57k duplicate invoice, and the 4.2k Momentum Ventures prepayment compel the UI to format EUR properly (`database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js:123` and `database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js:676`; `client/src/pages/Invoices.jsx:31`).
./PHASE_4_DEMO_REALISM_REPORT.md-21-- **Boundary dates:** SA-INV-2026-011 is due on 2026-04-30, the bank statement ends on 2026-04-30, and tax reports navigate Q1/Q2 so quarter-end rollups hit their cutoffs (`database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js:147`, `database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js:423`, and `database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js:739`).
./PHASE_4_DEMO_REALISM_REPORT.md:22:- **Safe copy and totals:** `View` components rely on `PageLoadingState`, `PageErrorState`, and `PageEmptyState` to keep copy consistent even when data is missing, and `formatCurrency`/`formatDate` ensure German formatting for totals and labels (`client/src/components/ui/PageStates.jsx:9` and `client/src/pages/Invoices.jsx:31`).

./docs/AUTHENTICATION_E2E.md-27-
./docs/AUTHENTICATION_E2E.md-28-## Rate-limit guidance for local dev
./docs/AUTHENTICATION_E2E.md:29:- The login rate limiter now honors `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` and `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (fallback to legacy `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT_*` for compatibility) and defaults to `15 minutes / 20 attempts` while running in `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`.
./docs/AUTHENTICATION_E2E.md:30:- Production uses `5 minutes / 5 attempts` out of the box but you can customize the window and cap via the environment variables above.
./docs/AUTHENTICATION_E2E.md-31-- When `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=true`, the limiter is skipped so local dev testing or automated smoke tests cannot be accidentally throttled.
./docs/AUTHENTICATION_E2E.md:32:- For faster recovery, enable the temporary reset route by setting `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_RESET_ENABLED=true`. An admin-authenticated client can then `POST /api/auth/rate-limit/reset` (body `{ "ip": "<address>" }` is optional; it defaults to the caller's IP) to clear the memory store for that client IP.
./docs/AUTHENTICATION_E2E.md:33:- The rate-limited middleware still returns `{ success: false, message: 'Too many login attempts…' }`, so the frontend surfaces a `rateLimit` flag from `AuthContext.login`. You may also log into the server shell and `export AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=true` when debugging a locked account to unblock yourself instantly.

./docs/Observability.md-23-
./docs/Observability.md-24-- When `METRICS_ENABLED=true`, each response updates an in-memory metrics snapshot (`src/middleware/metrics.js`) that tracks request count, latency, error rate, slow requests, and status code buckets. A minute-by-minute summary is emitted through `logger.performance`.
./docs/Observability.md:25:- The slow-request threshold is tunable via `LOG_SLOW_REQUEST_MS` (default `1000`), and slow routes are highlighted even when detailed request logging is disabled.
./docs/Observability.md-26-- The optional `REQUEST_LOGGING` flag controls whether every HTTP request emits an `info`/`warn`/`error` log; you can silence it to reduce noise while still preserving metric snapshots.
./docs/Observability.md-27-
--
./docs/Observability.md-37-  - `METRICS_ENABLED`: set to `true` to activate runtime metrics logging (defaults to `false`).
./docs/Observability.md-38-  - `REQUEST_LOGGING`: set to `false` if you want to keep the request log silent (defaults to `true`).
./docs/Observability.md:39:  - `LOG_SLOW_REQUEST_MS`: slow-request threshold in milliseconds (defaults to `1000`).
./docs/Observability.md:40:  - `LOG_SLOW_QUERY_MS`: slow-database-query threshold in milliseconds (defaults to `500`, set `0` to disable slow-query warnings).
./docs/Observability.md-41-  - `METRICS_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS`: snapshot cadence for runtime metrics (defaults to `60000`).
./docs/Observability.md-42-- `validateEnv.js` now warns when these are missing or set to unexpected values, but it never fails the startup — observability remains optional and toggleable.

(`client/src/components/TopBar.jsx:546-573`). **Fix:** remove or collapse the unsupported entries into a single placeholder until a real route exists; keep the dropdown focused on the one working action (`Logout`).
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md-5-- **Disabled control missing a tooltip** — the `Bookmarks` button has no `title`/`aria` description while the other disabled controls describe why they are inert (`client/src/components/TopBar.jsx:566-572`). **Fix:** add the same contextual tooltip (`title` or `aria-describedby`) or hide the control until the feature ships to avoid accessibility/UX gaps.

These strings sit next to translated labels, so they break localization and tone consistency. **Fix:** pull those strings into i18n keys and reuse them everywhere the user’s session status is described.

./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md-37-## 5 Profile & Account UX
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md:38:- **No implementation exists for the profile dropdown placeholders** — the menu shows “Profile”, “Settings”, and “Bookmarks”, yet the router never registers `/profile`, `/settings`, or `/bookmarks` routes (`client/src/App.jsx:32-220`). Keep the dropdown lean: primary actions (profile/settings), secondary contextual links (subscription, company switch), and a single logout CTA. Repeated disabled “coming soon” buttons dilute the experience (`client/src/components/TopBar.jsx:546-588`). **Fix:** streamline to a single list of working links and move explanatory text (e.g., role, subscription) into the header area of the menu instead of cluttering the controls.

./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md-41-## 6 Page State Consistency (Dashboard, Invoices, Expenses, Bank Statements)
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md:42:Each page should consistently present **loading**, **empty**, **error**, and **no-access** states with aligned copy/components.
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md-43-
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md:44:- **Dashboard** (`client/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx:86-143`): loading uses a `Skeleton`, which is more visually dense than the spinner used elsewhere; error uses `EmptyState` but the help copy is raw text; the disabled state uses bespoke copy instead of translation keys; the empty CTA (“Go to invoices”) is not localized. **Fix:** standardize on the same loading component or at least the same animation style, translate every state copy, and reuse shared components (e.g., `ErrorState`) for errors.
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md:45:- **Invoices** (`client/src/pages/Invoices.jsx:122-309`): the “select a company” state is the only no-access path, but other pages escalate to a more informative layout; error feedback is a bare `<div>` instead of `ErrorState`/`EmptyState`; empty-state CTA (“Create invoice”) is not translated; table headers and filters are hard-coded English strings. **Fix:** show the same `EmptyState` component for errors, translate all copy, and ensure the “no company” message lines up with the other pages.
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md-46-- **Expenses** (`client/src/pages/Expenses.jsx:73-149`): there is no guard when `activeCompany` is missing, so the page renders a blank table instead of an explicit no-access message; the read-only banner, empty state, table headers, and buttons are all literal English. **Fix:** detect `!activeCompany` and render the standard “select a company” `EmptyState`, translate the strings, and keep the read-only banner consistent with the other experience.
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_UI_UX_AUDIT.md:47:- **Bank Statements** (`client/src/pages/BankStatements.jsx:146-336`): loading uses a spinner, but error displays a plain `p` with `error.message`; empty state copy and CTA (“Upload Statement”) are not localized and even keeps the button disabled with a tooltip; preview/import action tooltips and helper sentences are hard-coded. **Fix:** reuse `EmptyState`/`ErrorState`, translate all copy, and surface consistent CTAs/disabled indicators for read-only users.

./docs/DR.md-28-
./docs/DR.md-29-### Immutable log recovery
./docs/DR.md:30:1. Use the latest encrypted backup and WAL archive to reconstruct the `audit_logs` table in an isolated environment.
./docs/DR.md-31-2. Run `node scripts/ops/verify/verify-restore.js` to ensure `AuditLogService.validateChain()` returns `true` before importing any data.
./docs/DR.md-32-3. If a broken log segment exists, do not edit it; instead, replay only the unaffected tail and start a new append-only sequence with a new `hash` (document the split for auditors).
--
./docs/DR.md-35-| Item | Recoverable? | Notes |
./docs/DR.md-36-| --- | --- | --- |
./docs/DR.md:37:| Postgres database snapshot | ✅ | Latest full dump plus WAL archive can rebuild all schema and rows. |
./docs/DR.md:38:| Point-in-time transactions | ✅ | WAL folders preserved by incremental script allow replay to a timestamp (see `point-in-time.sh`). |
./docs/DR.md-39-| Audit hash chain | ✅ | Hash chain validated by `scripts/ops/verify/verify-restore.js`; corrupted segments require replaying from the last known good log.
./docs/DR.md-40-| Application server state | ✅ | Rebuild from the tagged Docker image and redeploy; config secrets come from vault.
./docs/DR.md-41-| Encrypted backups | ✅ | Stored with AES-256 via `full-backup.sh`; rotate the passphrase and limit access to backups.
./docs/DR.md-42-| Real-time CPU/memory state | ❌ | Not recorded; restart from scratch.
./docs/DR.md:43:| Data written after the last WAL file | ❌ | Can only recover up to the latest WAL shipped; any unarchived transaction is lost.
./docs/DR.md-44-
./docs/DR.md-45-## Failover verification checklist
./docs/DR.md-46-- [ ] Latest full backup file exists in `backups/full` and was encrypted with the current passphrase.
./docs/DR.md:47:- [ ] WAL archive directory (`backups/wal`) contains segments that cover the time between backups.
./docs/DR.md:48:- [ ] `scripts/ops/restore/full-restore.sh` runs cleanly and restores data to a temporary database.
./docs/DR.md-49-- [ ] `scripts/ops/verify/verify-restore.js` reports valid audit hashes and expected row counts.
./docs/DR.md-50-- [ ] New database credentials and JWT secrets are rotated immediately after validation.

./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-7-### Unveränderbarkeit
./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-8-
./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md:9:- Die Tabelle `audit_logs` (database/migrations/20251225000400-create-audit-logs.js:5) protokolliert `timestamp`, `oldValues`, `newValues`, `hash` und `previousHash` für jeden Änderungsversuch; jede Zeile enthält zudem den verantwortlichen `userId`, den `resourceType`/`resourceId` und einen Default-`reason`, sodass der ursprüngliche Zustand nachvollziehbar bleibt.
./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-10-- Mit der Ergänzung der Spalte `immutable` (database/migrations/20260106000000-add-audit-log-immutable.js:5) und der CHECK-Bedingung `immutable IS TRUE` plus Default-`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` für `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (database/migrations/20260109001000-lock-audit-immutability.js:6) ist jede Audit-Zeile dauerhaft auf TRUE fixiert, wodurch nachträgliche Modifikationen oder das Zurücksetzen auf `false` scheitern.
./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-11-- Die Audit-Tabelle verwaltet seit der Nachrüstung von `companyId`, `requestId` und `metadata` (database/migrations/20260112000000-add-audit-log-company-requestid.js:13) obligatorisch die zugehörige Firma, eine fortlaufende Request-ID sowie optionale Metadaten, was revisionssichere Schreibvorgänge ermöglicht.

./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-50-### Audit Logs
./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-51-
./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md:52:Jeder Schreibzugriff erzeugt einen Audit-Eintrag mit `action`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `oldValues`, `newValues`, `userId`, `companyId` und `requestId` (database/migrations/20251225000400-create-audit-logs.js:5, database/migrations/20260112000000-add-audit-log-company-requestid.js:13). Die Einträge erhalten Hash- und Vorheriger-Hash-Ketten (database/migrations/20251225000400-create-audit-logs.js:61) und bleiben durch `immutable` fest auf TRUE gesetzt (database/migrations/20260106000000-add-audit-log-immutable.js:5), weshalb jeder Audit-Datensatz gegen missbräuchliche Änderung geschützt und jederzeit nachvollziehbar ist.

./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-4-
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-5-- **External attackers** seek to steal or forge JWTs, exploit weak RBAC, or force registration endpoints to run in production (see `src/services/authService.js:1-172`).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md:6:- **Malicious insiders** or compromised users could attempt privilege escalation by calling high-priv routes; `src/middleware/authMiddleware.js:1-60` enforces hierarchical RBAC (viewer→auditor→accountant→admin).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-7-- **Infrastructure faults** (DB downtime, missing columns) could suppress audit logs; `src/services/auditLogService.js:1-120` relies on an append-only hash chain, and every sensitive operation uses `withAuditLog` (`src/services/withAuditLog.js:1-20`), so failures roll back the request (fail-closed).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-8-- **Token replay** is feasible if revoked tokens remain in DB or refresh secrets are compromised; `src/services/revokedTokenService.js:1-31` and `src/services/authService.js:1-180` handle revocation and TTLs.
--
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-11-
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-12-- **JWT theft** – tokens grant `req.user` and `req.companyId` access; there is no refresh token rotation beyond revoking via `activeTokenService`/`revokedTokenService`, so key compromise grants ongoing access until expiry (30m default).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md:13:- **Brute-force login** – the `/api/auth/login` endpoint is limited to 5 attempts per 5 minutes via `authRateLimiter` in `src/middleware/security.js:70-110`, mitigating credential stuffing.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md:14:- **RBAC bypass** – controllers call `requireRole` (`src/middleware/authMiddleware.js:30-61`), but routes still import service helpers and share the same user object, so any bug that bypasses middleware (e.g., forgotten `requireRole` on new endpoint) could elevate privileges.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md:15:- **Audit log disablement** – `withAuditLog` re-throws if `AuditLogService.appendEntry` fails, so attackers cannot bypass logging; however, missing schema elements (e.g., `audit_logs.immutable` column not present) manifest as high-severity denial-of-service (fails every audited operation).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-16-- **Registration gating** – `authService.register` forbids production but the guard is based on `NODE_ENV`; a misconfigured env could re-enable registration, so configuration drift is an attack vector.
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-17-
--
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-21-- **Revocation & session management** store JWT IDs in `active_tokens` and `revoked_tokens` tables (`src/services/activeTokenService.js:1-27`, `src/services/revokedTokenService.js:1-30`), so logout/revocation is possible before expiration.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-22-- **Rate limiting & input hardening** in `src/middleware/security.js:1-240` wrap the API; the stack uses Helmet, body sanitizers, `mongoSanitize`, `xss-clean`, `hpp`, size limits, and per-route rate/speed limiters (auth, uploads, general API).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md:23:- **Fail-closed audit log** ensures GoBD compliance; `withAuditLog` waits for `appendEntry` and rolls back on failure (`src/services/withAuditLog.js:1-19`), enforcing accountability even if the database temporarily rejects writes.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_4_SECURITY.md-24-- **RBAC hierarchy** ensures admins always satisfy lower tiers (`src/middleware/authMiddleware.js:30-60`), simplifying permission checks while still allowing denials when `req.user` missing.

./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-3-## 1. UX pain points
./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-4-
./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md:5:- **Onboarding clarity:** `client/src/pages/OnboardingWizard.jsx` orchestrates a multi-step wizard, but several steps still render “Coming soon” cards (`client/src/components/PlaceholderCard.jsx`). Users who complete the profile step see no follow-up guidance—even the CTA defaults to `Next` without context—so first-time adopters are unsure whether they finished onboarding or need to wait.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-6-- **Mobile responsiveness:** Data-dense dashboards (`client/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx`, `Analytics.jsx`) rely on grid layouts with fixed column counts, so they overflow on screens narrower than ~900px. The `client/src/components/CardGrid.jsx` lacks responsive breakpoints, leaving controls partially hidden on tablets.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-7-- **Actionable error feedback:** `client/src/services/api.js` centralizes error formatting via `formatApiError`, which falls back to “An error occurred. Please try again.” This safe fallback obscures cause and prevents differentiating retryable vs permanent failures; surfaces only status codes (401, 403, 429, 5xx) but no backend `code`/`details` fields (see `formatApiError` lines 37-74).

./docs/audits/PHASE_3_ACCOUNTING.md:13:- **VAT rate enforcement:** `VatComplianceService` rejects non-standard rates or currencies, so even if a line item attempts to submit `vatRate=0.25` or `currency=USD`, the system raises `VAT_RATE_ILLEGAL` / `CURRENCY_ILLEGAL` before persisting.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_3_ACCOUNTING.md:14:- **Status transitions:** `invoiceService` only allows `DRAFT → SENT`, `SENT → {PAID, OVERDUE, CANCELLED}`, and `OVERDUE → {PAID, CANCELLED}`; the board prevents reopening `PAID` invoices. `expenseService` similarly only allows `draft → {booked, archived}` and `booked → archived`.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_3_ACCOUNTING.md-15-- **Missing fields in tax reporting:** `taxCalculator` insists on `Invoice.rawAttributes` containing `type`, `invoiceDate`, `vatRate`, etc., and queries statuses `[processed, approved, paid]`. ./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-6-
./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-7-- **Timeout enforcement** – `src/middleware/apiTimeout.js` installs `createApiTimeoutMiddleware` on every `/api` path (see `src/app.js`). It sets a 500 ms hard limit (customizable via `API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`), injects an `X-API-Timeout` header, and returns a `504 REQUEST_TIMEOUT` payload if the guardrail is triggered. There is a dedicated override for the dashboard namespace so `/api/dashboard/stats` gets an 800 ms budget (`API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DASHBOARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`).
./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md:8:- **Observability & slow-response logging** – the existing `response-time` middleware (threshold 1000 ms) captures duration, adds `X-Response-Time`, and records slow requests so any unexpected latency is visible in logs/monitoring.
./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-9-- **Error handling** – every route is wrapped in `try/catch` and `next(error)`, feeding into `src/middleware/errorHandler.js`, which ensures the client always receives a JSON `{ status:'error', message, requestId }` envelope, complete with operational codes + telemetry hooks when needed.
./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-10-- **Smoke verification** – `scripts/dev-smoke.js` drives `/health` + `/api/auth/login` + `/api/companies` + `/api/invoices` + `/api/ai/insights` to prove the core happy paths return successfully, which helps confirm no endpoint is silently hanging.

./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-62-- **AI insight schema incompleteness:** `database/migrations/20251230100000-create-ai-insights.js` plus `20251229100000-add-missing-aiinsight-columns.js` stop at `id`, timestamps, and six optional columns. `src/models/AIInsight.js` and the demo seeder (`database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js`) expect `companyId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `type`, `severity`, `confidenceScore`, `summary`, `why`, etc., and the app defines indexes on these columns. None exist, and `ai_insight_decisions` has no migration at all. This is a hard block: every AI insight/decision insert will fail with “column/relation does not exist”, effectively losing all AI-compliance telemetry.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-63-- **Tax report PK drift:** While `src/models/TaxReport.js` uses a UUID primary key, migration `20251225001000-create-tax-reports.js` still defines `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. `20251229101000-align-taxreport-id-type.js` only adds `id_new` UUID; it never backfills/migrates it to serve as the table’s PK or drops the integer `id`. Sequelize will therefore try to insert UUIDs into `id` and hit a type mismatch, making the entire tax report pipeline unable to persist new data (loss of reporting).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md:64:- **Nullability mismatch for expenses:** `Expense` model forbids NULLs on the demo-added columns (`category`, `netAmount`, `vatRate`, `vatAmount`, `grossAmount`, `createdByUserId`, `status`, `source`), yet `20251227000000-extend-demo-schema.js` created them as nullable without defaults. Rows that pre-date the extension (or import batches that omit those fields) will now fail validation when touched, obstructing migrations or services that touch legacy data.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-65-- **Demo seed safety:** `scripts/seed-demo-prod.js` enforces `DEMO_MODE=true` and `ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true`, resets `NODE_ENV` to `production`, runs `scripts/verify-schema.js`, and then invokes the guarded seeder. This prevents accidental seeding in production/staging. Demo seeding also relies on `AuditLogService`, so until the `immutable` column and AI tables are fixed, the seeder will blow up—meaning the guard is preventing further data loss.

./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-22-
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-23-- **Layered HTTP flow:** `src/app.js` centralizes middleware, docs (`src/config/swagger.js`), and health checks before handing requests to well-named route files, delivering a predictable entry route for every API surface.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:24:- **Services backed by clear models:** Routes such as `src/routes/bankStatements.js` invoke domain services like `src/services/bankStatementService.js`, while Sequelize models under `src/models/` expose associations via `src/models/index.js`, so persistence logic is kept in one folder (models) and business rules sit next to the domain flows (services).  
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-25-- **Robust environment/config handling:** `index.js` + `src/utils/validateEnv.js` guard required variables, `src/config/database.js`/`config/sequelize.js` choose Postgres vs SQLite, and `Dockerfile` + `docker-compose.prod.yml` rely on `.env.prod` + health checks to keep deployments consistent.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:26:- **Operational scaffolding:** Scripts such as `scripts/verify-schema.js`, `scripts/check-migrations.js`, and the `scripts/ops/` suite provide runnable gates for migrations, backups, and readiness; tests mirror production layers through `tests/fixtures`, `tests/integration`, and route/service-specific files.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-27-- **Observability and security baked in:** Structured logging (`src/lib/logger`), security middleware (`src/middleware/security.*`), RBAC helpers, request timing (`src/lib/logger.requestLogger`), and `/health`, `/ready`, `/metrics` endpoints give teams visibility across the same runtime used in production.
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-28-
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-29-## Weaknesses
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-30-
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:31:- **Controller-service boundary sometimes blurred:** Certain routes (`src/routes/bankStatements.js` brings models like `BankStatement`/`BankTransaction` into the route layer) still handle transactions directly, which duplicates persistence concerns and bypasses service-level invariants.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:32:- **Monolithic service classes:** Core services such as `src/services/bankStatementService.js` currently mix CSV/MT940/CAMT parsing, file I/O, transaction creation, summary assembly, and transactional fencing within one class, making it harder to unit-test, mock, or scale individual responsibilities.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-33-- **Limited background processing strategy:** Synchronous file parsing and business rules run inside HTTP request handlers (e.g., bank imports, AI insight generation) without a job queue or worker layer, meaning CPU-bound work blocks the Node event loop and risks timeouts under higher concurrency.  
./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-34-- **Configuration is environment-variable heavy with limited separation:** Every module loads `dotenv` (entry scripts plus `src/config/database.js`), so setups with multiple entry points must reapply the same overrides; there is no explicit config caching or typed schema beyond `validateEnv`, increasing the chance of drift between env files and runtime expectations.

./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-27-## Risk analysis & mitigation
./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-28-- **Risk:** A new automation detector or insight writer might forget to add explainability metadata or disclaimers, reintroducing legal ambiguity. **Mitigation:** service constructors (`aiInsightsService`, `recommendationBuilder`, `explainability.js`) define mandatory fields, and `tests/postgres/complianceConstraints.test.js` plus future code reviews must confirm those fields are not omitted.
./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md:29:- **Risk:** The AI audit trail could lose tenant context if `companyId` is disconnected from the user or if requests bypass `aiRouteGuard`. **Mitigation:** `aiRouteGuard` always injects `requestId`/`companyId` and rejects unauthorized users before any logging occurs, and the new schema enforces `companyId`/`requestId` at the DB level; plus `npm run test:postgres` checks the audit schema.
./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-30-- **Risk:** Automation suggestions might ever become authoritative if `requiresHumanApproval` is flipped. **Mitigation:** `automationContract`, `recommendationBuilder`, and `aiSuggestionService` hard-code `requiresHumanApproval: true` and runtime guards throw if mutated, so any sustainable change requires deliberate code modifications and test updates.

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8878-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-7-### Unveränderbarkeit
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8879-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-8-
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:8880:./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md:9:- Die Tabelle `audit_logs` (database/migrations/20251225000400-create-audit-logs.js:5) protokolliert `timestamp`, `oldValues`, `newValues`, `hash` und `previousHash` für jeden Änderungsversuch; jede Zeile enthält zudem den verantwortlichen `userId`, den `resourceType`/`resourceId` und einen Default-`reason`, sodass der ursprüngliche Zustand nachvollziehbar bleibt.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8881-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-10-- Mit der Ergänzung der Spalte `immutable` (database/migrations/20260106000000-add-audit-log-immutable.js:5) und der CHECK-Bedingung `immutable IS TRUE` plus Default-`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` für `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (database/migrations/20260109001000-lock-audit-immutability.js:6) ist jede Audit-Zeile dauerhaft auf TRUE fixiert, wodurch nachträgliche Modifikationen oder das Zurücksetzen auf `false` scheitern.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8882-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-11-- Die Audit-Tabelle verwaltet seit der Nachrüstung von `companyId`, `requestId` und `metadata` (database/migrations/20260112000000-add-audit-log-company-requestid.js:13) obligatorisch die zugehörige Firma, eine fortlaufende Request-ID sowie optionale Metadaten, was revisionssichere Schreibvorgänge ermöglicht.

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8884-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-50-### Audit Logs
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8885-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-51-
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:8886:./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md:52:Jeder Schreibzugriff erzeugt einen Audit-Eintrag mit `action`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `oldValues`, `newValues`, `userId`, `companyId` und `requestId` (database/migrations/20251225000400-create-audit-logs.js:5, database/migrations/20260112000000-add-audit-log-company-requestid.js:13). Die Einträge erhalten Hash- und Vorheriger-Hash-Ketten (database/migrations/20251225000400-create-audit-logs.js:61) und bleiben durch `immutable` fest auf TRUE gesetzt (database/migrations/20260106000000-add-audit-log-immutable.js:5), weshalb jeder Audit-Datensatz gegen missbräuchliche Änderung geschützt und jederzeit nachvollziehbar ist.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8887-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-53-
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8888-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-54-## 3. Schutz gegen Manipulation
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8889-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-55-
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:8890:./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md:56:- Die Datenbank erzwingt über `immutable`-Checks und Default-Timestamps, dass Audit-Logs weder nachträglich zurückgesetzt noch ohne Zeitstempel editiert werden können (database/migrations/20260109001000-lock-audit-immutability.js:6).
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8891-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-57-- Die Hash-Kette (`hash`, `previousHash`) in Kombination mit `requestId`/`companyId` verhindert das heimliche Überschreiben oder Entfernen von Audit-Einträgen, da jeder Eintrag eine schreibgeschützte Verbindung zu seinem Vorgänger erhält (database/migrations/20251225000400-create-audit-logs.js:61, database/migrations/20260112000000-add-audit-log-company-requestid.js:24).
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-8892-./GOBD_COMPLIANCE_STATEMENT.md-58-- Spread-Summen und Status-Enum-Checks in `expenses`, `invoices`, `transactions` und `tax_reports` verbieten stille Änderungen, da inkonsistente Beträge, leere `status`-Werte oder nicht definierte Tax-Report-Zustände nicht gespeichert werden dürfen (database/migrations/20260108001000-add-financial-integrity-checks.js:3, database/migrations/20260109002000-lock-tax-report-status.js:7).

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-10621-./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-3-## 1. UX pain points
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-10622-./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-4-
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:10623:./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md:5:- **Onboarding clarity:** `client/src/pages/OnboardingWizard.jsx` orchestrates a multi-step wizard, but several steps still render “Coming soon” cards (`client/src/components/PlaceholderCard.jsx`). Users who complete the profile step see no follow-up guidance—even the CTA defaults to `Next` without context—so first-time adopters are unsure whether they finished onboarding or need to wait.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-10624-./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-6-- **Mobile responsiveness:** Data-dense dashboards (`client/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx`, `Analytics.jsx`) rely on grid layouts with fixed column counts, so they overflow on screens narrower than ~900px. The `client/src/components/CardGrid.jsx` lacks responsive breakpoints, leaving controls partially hidden on tablets.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-10625-./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-7-- **Actionable error feedback:** `client/src/services/api.js` centralizes error formatting via `formatApiError`, which falls back to “An error occurred. Please try again.” This safe fallback obscures cause and prevents differentiating retryable vs permanent failures; surfaces only status codes (401, 403, 429, 5xx) but no backend `code`/`details` fields (see `formatApiError` lines 37-74).

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-10971-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-62-- **AI insight schema incompleteness:** `database/migrations/20251230100000-create-ai-insights.js` plus `20251229100000-add-missing-aiinsight-columns.js` stop at `id`, timestamps, and six optional columns. `src/models/AIInsight.js` and the demo seeder (`database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js`) expect `companyId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `type`, `severity`, `confidenceScore`, `summary`, `why`, etc., and the app defines indexes on these columns. None exist, and `ai_insight_decisions` has no migration at all. This is a hard block: every AI insight/decision insert will fail with “column/relation does not exist”, effectively losing all AI-compliance telemetry.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-10972-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-63-- **Tax report PK drift:** While `src/models/TaxReport.js` uses a UUID primary key, migration `20251225001000-create-tax-reports.js` still defines `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. `20251229101000-align-taxreport-id-type.js` only adds `id_new` UUID; it never backfills/migrates it to serve as the table’s PK or drops the integer `id`. Sequelize will therefore try to insert UUIDs into `id` and hit a type mismatch, making the entire tax report pipeline unable to persist new data (loss of reporting).  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:10973:./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md:64:- **Nullability mismatch for expenses:** `Expense` model forbids NULLs on the demo-added columns (`category`, `netAmount`, `vatRate`, `vatAmount`, `grossAmount`, `createdByUserId`, `status`, `source`), yet `20251227000000-extend-demo-schema.js` created them as nullable without defaults. Rows that pre-date the extension (or import batches that omit those fields) will now fail validation when touched, obstructing migrations or services that touch legacy data.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-10974-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-65-- **Demo seed safety:** `scripts/seed-demo-prod.js` enforces `DEMO_MODE=true` and `ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true`, resets `NODE_ENV` to `production`, runs `scripts/verify-schema.js`, and then invokes the guarded seeder. This prevents accidental seeding in production/staging. Demo seeding also relies on `AuditLogService`, so until the `immutable` column and AI tables are fixed, the seeder will blow up—meaning the guard is preventing further data loss.

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:11696:./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:31:- **Controller-service boundary sometimes blurred:** Certain routes (`src/routes/bankStatements.js` brings models like `BankStatement`/`BankTransaction` into the route layer) still handle transactions directly, which duplicates persistence concerns and bypasses service-level invariants.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:11697:./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:32:- **Monolithic service classes:** Core services such as `src/services/bankStatementService.js` currently mix CSV/MT940/CAMT parsing, file I/O, transaction creation, summary assembly, and transactional fencing within one class, making it harder to unit-test, mock, or scale individual responsibilities.

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-13129-./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-7-- **Timeout enforcement** – `src/middleware/apiTimeout.js` installs `createApiTimeoutMiddleware` on every `/api` path (see `src/app.js`). It sets a 500 ms hard limit (customizable via `API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`), injects an `X-API-Timeout` header, and returns a `504 REQUEST_TIMEOUT` payload if the guardrail is triggered. There is a dedicated override for the dashboard namespace so `/api/dashboard/stats` gets an 800 ms budget (`API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DASHBOARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`).

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-13131-./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-9-- **Error handling** – every route is wrapped in `try/catch` and `next(error)`, feeding into `src/middleware/errorHandler.js`, which ensures the client always receives a JSON `{ status:'error', message, requestId }` envelope, complete with operational codes + telemetry hooks when needed.

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-21168-./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-3-## Overview
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-21169-./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-4-- Full logical backups run via `scripts/ops/backup/full-backup.sh`, producing AES-256 encrypted `sql.gz.enc` artifacts in `backups/full`.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:21170:./docs/operations/backup-restore.md:5:- Incremental durability is provided by streaming WAL segments with `scripts/ops/backup/incremental-wal.sh`, which writes to `backups/wal`. A replication slot (default `smartaccounting_slot`) keeps the WAL archive continuous.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-21171-./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-6-- All backups are immutable and encrypted at rest; the passphrase is never stored with the artifact and must be supplied via `BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` when running scripts.

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-21175-./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-27-## Point-in-time recovery
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:21176:./docs/operations/backup-restore.md:28:- WAL streaming keeps the RPO low. ./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-34620-./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-76866-./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-31443-docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-63-- **Tax report PK drift:** While `src/models/TaxReport.js` uses a UUID primary key, migration `20251225001000-create-tax-reports.js` still defines `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. `20251229101000-align-taxreport-id-type.js` only adds `id_new` UUID; it never backfills/migrates it to serve as the table’s PK or drops the integer `id`. ./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-40924-./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-83555-./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-72466-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-63-- **Tax report PK drift:** While `src/models/TaxReport.js` uses a UUID primary key, migration `20251225001000-create-tax-reports.js` still defines `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. `20251229101000-align-taxreport-id-type.js` only adds `id_new` UUID; it never backfills/migrates it to serve as the table’s PK or drops the integer `id`. ./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-46562-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-27-## Risk analysis & mitigation
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-46563-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-28-- **Risk:** A new automation detector or insight writer might forget to add explainability metadata or disclaimers, reintroducing legal ambiguity. **Mitigation:** service constructors (`aiInsightsService`, `recommendationBuilder`, `explainability.js`) define mandatory fields, and `tests/postgres/complianceConstraints.test.js` plus future code reviews must confirm those fields are not omitted.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:46564:./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md:29:- **Risk:** The AI audit trail could lose tenant context if `companyId` is disconnected from the user or if requests bypass `aiRouteGuard`. **Mitigation:** `aiRouteGuard` always injects `requestId`/`companyId` and rejects unauthorized users before any logging occurs, and the new schema enforces `companyId`/`requestId` at the DB level; plus `npm run test:postgres` checks the audit schema.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-46565-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-30-- **Risk:** Automation suggestions might ever become authoritative if `requiresHumanApproval` is flipped. **Mitigation:** `automationContract`, `recommendationBuilder`, and `aiSuggestionService` hard-code `requiresHumanApproval: true` and runtime guards throw if mutated, so any sustainable change requires deliberate code modifications and test updates.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt-46566-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-31-
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH/TRUTH_AUDIT_20260630_075520.txt:46567:./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md:32:## The database enforces the law. The application cannot bypass it. AI is advisory-only and legally constrained.

The `client/src/components/CardGrid.jsx` lacks responsive breakpoints, leaving controls partially hidden on tablets.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt-17896-./docs/audits/PHASE_8_UX_DX.md-7-- **Actionable error feedback:** `client/src/services/api.js` centralizes error formatting via `formatApiError`, which falls back to “An error occurred. ./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt-18324-./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-7-- **Timeout enforcement** – `src/middleware/apiTimeout.js` installs `createApiTimeoutMiddleware` on every `/api` path (see `src/app.js`). It sets a 500 ms hard limit (customizable via `API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`), injects an `X-API-Timeout` header, and returns a `504 REQUEST_TIMEOUT` payload if the guardrail is triggered. There is a dedicated override for the dashboard namespace so `/api/dashboard/stats` gets an 800 ms budget (`API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DASHBOARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`).

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt-18342-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-62-- **AI insight schema incompleteness:** `database/migrations/20251230100000-create-ai-insights.js` plus `20251229100000-add-missing-aiinsight-columns.js` stop at `id`, timestamps, and six optional columns. `src/models/AIInsight.js` and the demo seeder (`database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js`) expect `companyId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `type`, `severity`, `confidenceScore`, `summary`, `why`, etc., and the app defines indexes on these columns. None exist, and `ai_insight_decisions` has no migration at all. This is a hard block: every AI insight/decision insert will fail with “column/relation does not exist”, effectively losing all AI-compliance telemetry.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt-18343-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-63-- **Tax report PK drift:** While `src/models/TaxReport.js` uses a UUID primary key, migration `20251225001000-create-tax-reports.js` still defines `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. `20251229101000-align-taxreport-id-type.js` only adds `id_new` UUID; it never backfills/migrates it to serve as the table’s PK or drops the integer `id`. Sequelize will therefore try to insert UUIDs into `id` and hit a type mismatch, making the entire tax report pipeline unable to persist new data (loss of reporting).  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt:18344:./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md:64:- **Nullability mismatch for expenses:** `Expense` model forbids NULLs on the demo-added columns (`category`, `netAmount`, `vatRate`, `vatAmount`, `grossAmount`, `createdByUserId`, `status`, `source`), yet `20251227000000-extend-demo-schema.js` created them as nullable without defaults. Rows that pre-date the extension (or import batches that omit those fields) will now fail validation when touched, obstructing migrations or services that touch legacy data.  
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt-18345-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-65-- **Demo seed safety:** `scripts/seed-demo-prod.js` enforces `DEMO_MODE=true` and `ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true`, resets `NODE_ENV` to `production`, runs `scripts/verify-schema.js`, and then invokes the guarded seeder. This prevents accidental seeding in production/staging. Demo seeding also relies on `AuditLogService`, so until the `immutable` column and AI tables are fixed, the seeder will blow up—meaning the guard is preventing further data loss.

./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt-18931-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-28-- **Risk:** A new automation detector or insight writer might forget to add explainability metadata or disclaimers, reintroducing legal ambiguity. **Mitigation:** service constructors (`aiInsightsService`, `recommendationBuilder`, `explainability.js`) define mandatory fields, and `tests/postgres/complianceConstraints.test.js` plus future code reviews must confirm those fields are not omitted.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt:18932:./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md:29:- **Risk:** The AI audit trail could lose tenant context if `companyId` is disconnected from the user or if requests bypass `aiRouteGuard`. **Mitigation:** `aiRouteGuard` always injects `requestId`/`companyId` and rejects unauthorized users before any logging occurs, and the new schema enforces `companyId`/`requestId` at the DB level; plus `npm run test:postgres` checks the audit schema.
./docs/AUDIT/TRUTH_FINAL_CHECK/FINAL_TRUTH_20260630_084251.txt-18933-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-30-- **Risk:** Automation suggestions might ever become authoritative if `requiresHumanApproval` is flipped. **Mitigation:** `automationContract`, `recommendationBuilder`, and `aiSuggestionService` hard-code `requiresHumanApproval: true` and runtime guards throw if mutated, so any sustainable change requires deliberate code modifications and test updates.

./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-31442-docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md:62:- **AI insight schema incompleteness:** `database/migrations/20251230100000-create-ai-insights.js` plus `20251229100000-add-missing-aiinsight-columns.js` stop at `id`, timestamps, and six optional columns. `src/models/AIInsight.js` and the demo seeder (`database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js`) expect `companyId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `type`, `severity`, `confidenceScore`, `summary`, `why`, etc., and the app defines indexes on these columns. None exist, and `ai_insight_decisions` has no migration at all. This is a hard block: every AI insight/decision insert will fail with “column/relation does not exist”, effectively losing all AI-compliance telemetry.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-31443-docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-63-- **Tax report PK drift:** While `src/models/TaxReport.js` uses a UUID primary key, migration `20251225001000-create-tax-reports.js` still defines `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. `20251229101000-align-taxreport-id-type.js` only adds `id_new` UUID; it never backfills/migrates it to serve as the table’s PK or drops the integer `id`. Sequelize will therefore try to insert UUIDs into `id` and hit a type mismatch, making the entire tax report pipeline unable to persist new data (loss of reporting).  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:31444:docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-64-- **Nullability mismatch for expenses:** `Expense` model forbids NULLs on the demo-added columns (`category`, `netAmount`, `vatRate`, `vatAmount`, `grossAmount`, `createdByUserId`, `status`, `source`), yet `20251227000000-extend-demo-schema.js` created them as nullable without defaults. Rows that pre-date the extension (or import batches that omit those fields) will now fail validation when touched, obstructing migrations or services that touch legacy data.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-31445-docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md:65:- **Demo seed safety:** `scripts/seed-demo-prod.js` enforces `DEMO_MODE=true` and `ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true`, resets `NODE_ENV` to `production`, runs `scripts/verify-schema.js`, and then invokes the guarded seeder. This prevents accidental seeding in production/staging. Demo seeding also relies on `AuditLogService`, so until the `immutable` column and AI tables are fixed, the seeder will blow up—meaning the guard is preventing further data loss.

./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-35693-docs/audits/PHASE_3_ACCOUNTING.md-12-- **Net-vs-gross entry:** `expenseService` tolerates the caller providing only `grossAmount` and back-calculates `net`/`vat` (and vice versa) while still coercing both to two decimal places so rounding never drifts beyond cents.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:35694:docs/audits/PHASE_3_ACCOUNTING.md-13-- **VAT rate enforcement:** `VatComplianceService` rejects non-standard rates or currencies, so even if a line item attempts to submit `vatRate=0.25` or `currency=USD`, the system raises `VAT_RATE_ILLEGAL` / `CURRENCY_ILLEGAL` before persisting.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:35695:docs/audits/PHASE_3_ACCOUNTING.md:14:- **Status transitions:** `invoiceService` only allows `DRAFT → SENT`, `SENT → {PAID, OVERDUE, CANCELLED}`, and `OVERDUE → {PAID, CANCELLED}`; the board prevents reopening `PAID` invoices. `expenseService` similarly only allows `draft → {booked, archived}` and `booked → archived`.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-35696-docs/audits/PHASE_3_ACCOUNTING.md-15-- **Missing fields in tax reporting:** `taxCalculator` insists on `Invoice.rawAttributes` containing `type`, `invoiceDate`, `vatRate`, etc., and queries statuses `[processed, approved, paid]`. The current `Invoice` model only defines `date`, `status` (uppercase values), and no `type`, so `calculateUstReport` immediately throws `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` and never reaches legal aggregation logic.

./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-72465-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-62-- **AI insight schema incompleteness:** `database/migrations/20251230100000-create-ai-insights.js` plus `20251229100000-add-missing-aiinsight-columns.js` stop at `id`, timestamps, and six optional columns. `src/models/AIInsight.js` and the demo seeder (`database/seeders/demo/20251226-demo-seed.js`) expect `companyId`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `type`, `severity`, `confidenceScore`, `summary`, `why`, etc., and the app defines indexes on these columns. None exist, and `ai_insight_decisions` has no migration at all. This is a hard block: every AI insight/decision insert will fail with “column/relation does not exist”, effectively losing all AI-compliance telemetry.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-72466-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-63-- **Tax report PK drift:** While `src/models/TaxReport.js` uses a UUID primary key, migration `20251225001000-create-tax-reports.js` still defines `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`. `20251229101000-align-taxreport-id-type.js` only adds `id_new` UUID; it never backfills/migrates it to serve as the table’s PK or drops the integer `id`. Sequelize will therefore try to insert UUIDs into `id` and hit a type mismatch, making the entire tax report pipeline unable to persist new data (loss of reporting).  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:72467:./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md:64:- **Nullability mismatch for expenses:** `Expense` model forbids NULLs on the demo-added columns (`category`, `netAmount`, `vatRate`, `vatAmount`, `grossAmount`, `createdByUserId`, `status`, `source`), yet `20251227000000-extend-demo-schema.js` created them as nullable without defaults. Rows that pre-date the extension (or import batches that omit those fields) will now fail validation when touched, obstructing migrations or services that touch legacy data.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-72468-./docs/audits/PHASE_2_DATABASE.md-65-- **Demo seed safety:** `scripts/seed-demo-prod.js` enforces `DEMO_MODE=true` and `ALLOW_DEMO_SEED=true`, resets `NODE_ENV` to `production`, runs `scripts/verify-schema.js`, and then invokes the guarded seeder. This prevents accidental seeding in production/staging. Demo seeding also relies on `AuditLogService`, so until the `immutable` column and AI tables are fixed, the seeder will blow up—meaning the guard is preventing further data loss.

./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-72827-./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-30-
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:72828:./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:31:- **Controller-service boundary sometimes blurred:** Certain routes (`src/routes/bankStatements.js` brings models like `BankStatement`/`BankTransaction` into the route layer) still handle transactions directly, which duplicates persistence concerns and bypasses service-level invariants.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:72829:./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:32:- **Monolithic service classes:** Core services such as `src/services/bankStatementService.js` currently mix CSV/MT940/CAMT parsing, file I/O, transaction creation, summary assembly, and transactional fencing within one class, making it harder to unit-test, mock, or scale individual responsibilities.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-72830-./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-33-- **Limited background processing strategy:** Synchronous file parsing and business rules run inside HTTP request handlers (e.g., bank imports, AI insight generation) without a job queue or worker layer, meaning CPU-bound work blocks the Node event loop and risks timeouts under higher concurrency.  
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-72831-./docs/audits/PHASE_1_ARCHITECTURE.md-34-- **Configuration is environment-variable heavy with limited separation:** Every module loads `dotenv` (entry scripts plus `src/config/database.js`), so setups with multiple entry points must reapply the same overrides; there is no explicit config caching or typed schema beyond `validateEnv`, increasing the chance of drift between env files and runtime expectations.

./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-73587-./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-7-- **Timeout enforcement** – `src/middleware/apiTimeout.js` installs `createApiTimeoutMiddleware` on every `/api` path (see `src/app.js`). It sets a 500 ms hard limit (customizable via `API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`), injects an `X-API-Timeout` header, and returns a `504 REQUEST_TIMEOUT` payload if the guardrail is triggered. There is a dedicated override for the dashboard namespace so `/api/dashboard/stats` gets an 800 ms budget (`API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DASHBOARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`).
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:73588:./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md:8:- **Observability & slow-response logging** – the existing `response-time` middleware (threshold 1000 ms) captures duration, adds `X-Response-Time`, and records slow requests so any unexpected latency is visible in logs/monitoring.
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-73589-./docs/PHASE_3_API_ROUTE_INVENTORY.md-9-- **Error handling** – every route is wrapped in `try/catch` and `next(error)`, feeding into `src/middleware/errorHandler.js`, which ensures the client always receives a JSON `{ status:'error', message, requestId }` envelope, complete with operational codes + telemetry hooks when needed.

./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-73626-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-27-## Risk analysis & mitigation
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-73627-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-28-- **Risk:** A new automation detector or insight writer might forget to add explainability metadata or disclaimers, reintroducing legal ambiguity. **Mitigation:** service constructors (`aiInsightsService`, `recommendationBuilder`, `explainability.js`) define mandatory fields, and `tests/postgres/complianceConstraints.test.js` plus future code reviews must confirm those fields are not omitted.
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt:73628:./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md:29:- **Risk:** The AI audit trail could lose tenant context if `companyId` is disconnected from the user or if requests bypass `aiRouteGuard`. **Mitigation:** `aiRouteGuard` always injects `requestId`/`companyId` and rejects unauthorized users before any logging occurs, and the new schema enforces `companyId`/`requestId` at the DB level; plus `npm run test:postgres` checks the audit schema.
./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-73629-./docs/compliance/AI_COMPLIANCE_REPORT_2026.md-30-- **Risk:** Automation suggestions might ever become authoritative if `requiresHumanApproval` is flipped. **Mitigation:** `automationContract`, `recommendationBuilder`, and `aiSuggestionService` hard-code `requiresHumanApproval: true` and runtime guards throw if mutated, so any sustainable change requires deliberate code modifications and test updates.

./docs/AUDIT/runtime/DEEP_AUDIT_RAW_20260629_220817.txt-84287-./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-27-## Point-in-time recovery

./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-3-## Overview
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-4-- Full logical backups run via `scripts/ops/backup/full-backup.sh`, producing AES-256 encrypted `sql.gz.enc` artifacts in `backups/full`.
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md:5:- Incremental durability is provided by streaming WAL segments with `scripts/ops/backup/incremental-wal.sh`, which writes to `backups/wal`. A replication slot (default `smartaccounting_slot`) keeps the WAL archive continuous.
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-6-- All backups are immutable and encrypted at rest; the passphrase is never stored with the artifact and must be supplied via `BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` when running scripts.
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-7-
--
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-26-
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-27-## Point-in-time recovery
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md:28:- WAL streaming keeps the RPO low. When you need to jump to a specific moment, replay the WAL files with `restore_command = 'cp "$WAL_ARCHIVE_DIR/%f" "%p"'` and configure `recovery_target_time` (the template script sets it for you).
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-29-- Always check the `buildMetadata.commitHash` in `/api/system/version` after the recovery to ensure the backend that attaches to the restored database matches the approved release.
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-30-
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-31-## Verification checklist
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-32-- [ ] Exported backups are encrypted (`scripts/ops/backup/full-backup.sh` succeeds).<br>
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md:33:- [ ] WAL archive includes segments for the targeted window (`backups/wal`).<br>
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-34-- [ ] Restore completes to a staging database using `scripts/ops/restore/full-restore.sh` without errors.<br>
./docs/operations/backup-restore.md-35-- [ ] Point-in-time exercises use `scripts/ops/restore/point-in-time.sh` and contain a `recovery.signal` file before promotion.<br>

src/services/ai/README.md-3-## Active components
src/services/ai/README.md:4:- `aiReadGateway.js` orchestrates every `/api/ai` read request, enforces read-only contracts, attaches disclaimers, and now logs the `requestId`/`companyId` pair into the immutable audit trail.
src/services/ai/README.md:5:- `aiAuditLogger.js` is the single audit bag for AI queries, responses, sessions, rate limits, and suggestions; it now persists `requestId`, `companyId`, and structured metadata for every entry.
src/services/ai/README.md-6-- `governance.js`, `contextContract.js`, `mutationIntent.js`, `promptRegistry.js`, `explainability.js`, and `insightTypes.js` form the compliance toolbox that redacts PII, enforces purpose/policy, detects mutation intent, and surfaces explainability data.
src/services/ai/README.md-7-- `aiDataService.js`, `aiAssistantService.js`, and `aiSuggestionService.js` contain the read-only AI handlers (summaries, assistant prompts, suggestions) and all bubble through `requiresHumanApproval`/`rateLimit` guards before returning advisory-only responses.
src/services/ai/README.md-8-- `aiInsightsService.js` covers insight generation, listing, exporting, and user decision recording (with explainable metadata) while checking company flags and schema integrity.
src/services/ai/README.md:9:- `automation/` contains the guarded automation pipeline (`automationGuard.js`, `automationEngine.js`, `automationAuditLogger.js`) plus the detectors/recommendation builder; all run in GET-only mode, log via `aiAuditLogger`, and require human approval for every proposed action.
